sentences.text:
The petitioners in both the petitions are before this Court seeking for the following reliefs:
"Quash the FIR in CR.Nos.9/2018 and 8/2018 respectively in both the cases of Electronic City Police Station, Bangalore City and quash the FIR in Cr.No.09/2018 Chief Judicial Magistrate (CJM) Bangalore Rural District, Bangalore, which has been registered against the petitioners for the offences punishable under Sections 143,147,149,447, 448,420,468,471,465,506 of IPC."
2.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
The complainant has given a first information on 10.01.2018 on the basis of which Crime Nos.
9/2018 and 8/2018 respectively in both the cases registered for the offences punishable under Sections 506, 143, 447, 420, 147, 149, 468, 448, 471 and 465 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (hereinafter referred to as 'IPC' for short).

The allegation made in the said complaint is that the property in Survey No.102/5 of the Begur village originally belonged to petitioner Nos.1 and 2, who had executed a power of attorney in favour of B. Adbul Kareem, S. Ameer Basha and Shaik Imtiaz, who had sold a site carved at of the said property in favour of the complainant in the year 2006.

The petitioner Nos.1 and 2 had approached the site owners including respondent No.1 in both the cases on 09.01.2008 demanding that each of them make payment to a sum of Rs.80/- per square feet, if they wanted to enjoy the site which have been sold in their favour and it is in this background it is contended that the aforesaid offences have been committed.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioners would submit that though the power of attorney had been executed in favour of the aforesaid B. Adbul Kareem, S. Ameer Basha and Shaik Imtiaz, the said power of attorney NC: 2024:KHC:10853 had been revoked and cancelled and as such, they did not have any power to execute the sale deed and on that basis he submits that the petitioners continuing to be in possession of the property, the petitioners themselves had lodged a complaint on 09.01.2018 alleging that respondent No.1 in both the cases with the aid of the Electronic City Police Inspector, who were seeking to trespass on the property of the petitioners and dispossesses the petitioners and in that background, action was sought for against the said persons.

On these grounds, he submits that the complaint filed by the petitioners prior to the complaint filed by respondent No.1 in both the cases is false and fabricated and is based on false and fabricated story and as such, the proceedings ought to be quashed.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioners would further submit that petitioner No.3 had filed a suit in O.S. No.455/2013 against petitioner Nos.1 and 2 and the NC: 2024:KHC:10853 power of attorney holders, the defendants not having entered appearance, the suit came to be decreed in favour of petitioner No.3 restraining the defendants therein in any manner interfering with the possession of petitioner No.2 in respect of Survey No.102/5 measuring 1 Acres and 20 guntas and another portion of Survey No.102/5 measuring 20 guntas.
6. Petitioner No.3 has also filed another suit in O.S. No.63/2015 against alleged purchasers of the sites.

An order of injunction has been granted against the alleged purchasers interfering with the possession of the petitioners and it is in that background, a complaint dated 09.01.2018 had been filed by the petitioners.
His submission is that the decree of permanent injunction has been passed in favour of the petitioners.

The respondents, claim that the defendants in the suit in O.S.
No.455/2013, could not have been filed a complaint impugned in the present matter.

Sri. Dinesh Rao, learned counsel for respondent No.1 in both the cases would submits that respondent No.1 in both the cases is the purchaser of the site in the aforesaid Survey No.102/5 apart from respondent No.1 in both the cases, there are several other purchasers, who are arraigned as defendants in O.S. No.63/2015.

All of them being in possession, the petitioners are seeking to extort money from the purchasers and it is in that background, a complaint had been filed, which is under challenge and as such, only due to the impugned order, investigation has stopped, if the impugned order is vacated, the above petition is dismissed, the investigation would go on, which would bring out the truth of the matter.

As such, he submits that the mater is not civil in nature as contended by the learned counsel for the petitioners, there being various ingredients of criminal offences as alleged, the matter needs to proceed with investigation.

Heard Sri. Manjunath B. R., learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri. Chowda Reddy, learned counsel and Sri. Dinesh Rao., learned counsel for respondent No.1 and Sri. M. R. Patil, learned HCGP for respondent No.2 in both the cases.
Perused the records in both the cases.

9. It is not in dispute that petitioner Nos. 1 and 2 have executed power of attorney in favour of B.
Adbul Kareem, S. Ameer Basha and Shaik Imtiaz authorizing them to form layout and sell the sites in the said layout.
Petitioner Nos.1 and 2 have subsequently sold the entire property to petitioner No.3, who had filed a suit in O.S. No.455/2013.

Petitioner No.1 was arraigned as defendant No.1,
petitioner No.2 was arraigned as defendant No.2 and the aforesaid three power of attorney holders were arraigned as defendant Nos.3 to 5.
Shockingly, petitioner Nos. 1 and 2, did not appear in the said suit.

They neither supported nor contested the claim - 10 - Bayya Reddy vs Smt Teresa Thomas @ Thresiyamma on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18015527/
5 NC: 2024:KHC:10853 of petitioner No.3 in the said suit.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: When petitioner No.3 is alleging that petitioner Nos.1 and 2 are illegally interfering with the alleged possession of petitioner No.3, on account of defendant Nos.1 and 2 forming a layout.
It is interesting to note that the present petition has been filed by Petitioner No.1 to 3 together.

Defendant Nos.3 to 5 power of attorney holders did not appear in the said suit it is in this background, that the suit for permanent injunction in O.S.
No.455/2013 came to be decreed on 08.07.2015, since there was no opposition.

10. The fact that the petitioner No.3 has also filed a suit in O.S. No.63/2015 on 23.12.2014 against the purchasers of the sites, would also establish that petitioner No.3 has taken cognizance of the purchase of the plots.
It cannot now be said that the allegations made by respondent No.1 in the impugned complaint is as regards civil dispute as contended by the learned counsel for the petitioners.

The manner in which the suit in O.S. No.455/2013 was filed and a decree passed therein without the defendants appearing and in the meanwhile O.S. No.63/2015 has been filed against the purchasers, who had purchased the property through the power of attorney holders of defendant Nos.1 and 2 therein, who are petitioner Nos.1 and 2 herein prima facie at this stage indicates the allegations made against them to be plausible.
11.

Hence, I am unable to accept the submissions of the learned counsel for the petitioners that the dispute is civil in nature; the matter would require proper investigation to bring out the truth in the matter when serious allegations are made against the petitioners.
In that view of the matter, no grounds have been made out.
The petitions stand dismissed.

12. Electronic City Police Station is directed to proceed with the investigation in FIR Nos.9/2018 and 8/2018 - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC:10853 respectively in both the cases and submit their reports at the earliest within a period of six months from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
Pending I.A.'s are disposed of in both the cases.
